title: 2008 AMC 10A Problem 9
statement:
Suppose that

\[ \dfrac{2x}{3} - \dfrac{x}{6} \]

is an integer. Which of the following statements must be true about \(x?\)

answerChoices.label: B
answerChoices.text:
It is even, but not necessarily a multiple of
\(3.\)

answerChoices.label: C
answerChoices.text: It is a multiple of \(3,\) but not necessarily even.

answerChoices.label: D
answerChoices.text:
It is a multiple of \(6,\) but not necessarily a multiple of
\(12.\)

solutions.text:
Combining over a common denominator, \(\dfrac{2x}{3} - \dfrac{x}{6} = \dfrac{4x - x}{6} = \dfrac{x}{2}.\)

For \(\dfrac{x}{2}\) to be an integer, \(x\) must be even.

The example \(x = 4\) shows that \(x\) need not be a multiple of \(3\) and rules out the other statements.

Thus, the correct answer is B.
hints: The expression simplifies to \(\dfrac{x}{2};\) decide what that being an integer forces about \(x\)
